scope.selection: Three AMQ-Bench mini30 samples whose original D1 service health failed for distinct packaging causes: undeclared transitive dependency, package-relative/local import handling, and installed-package shadowing plus dependency API drift.

baseline.failure: The submitted rdkit source directory shadowed the installed rdkit distribution and could not import rdBase.

allDeclaredProperties.failure: formal_charge returned null because the generated compatibility shim called a non-existent molecule method and the submitted algorithm converted that exception to None.

implementedGates: Separate static and runtime repair budgets with audited attempt counters.
Transitive import dependency preflight across reachable local modules.
Low-priority algorithm import paths to prevent submitted source directories from shadowing installed distributions.
Isolated Docker build, MCP registry discovery, per-tool smoke execution, output-schema validation, and partial smoke result preservation.
Runtime dependency API capability preflight that reports all missing imported attributes in one repair round.
Structured success=false failure-contract detection requiring adapters to raise MCP errors.
CPU-only dependency split, non-root runtime, no-network probe, read-only filesystem, capability drop, and resource limits.

conclusion.engineeringRecovery: The targeted runtime gate converted all three selected baseline health failures into container-startable MCP artifacts.
conclusion.functionalEvidence: RDKit moved from one mechanically exposed tool and failed startup to five registered tools with five successful primary-path smoke tests.
conclusion.remainingLimitation: Per-tool smoke coverage is not parameter-branch coverage. The extended RDKit check found one silent null result, so this targeted result must not be presented as proof that arbitrary template-compliant repositories are fully production-ready.
conclusion.nextGate: Support multiple evidence-backed smoke cases and semantic assertions per tool, then rerun the full mini30 set before claiming production readiness.
